description: Hi! We're a team made of high schoolers who want to make a solution to the visibility and monitoring of health in space, an interface that can update dependent of internal or external changes which also updates live
summary: Astrah Care is an advanced digital wellness and monitoring platform designed for space missions, bridging the gap between individual astronaut health tracking and collaborative crew well-being in extraterrestrial environments. By integrating real-time physiological data with spacecraft environmental and situational analytics, the interface provides a holistic, dynamic view of team health.
details:
Astrah Care is an offline-first, autonomous medical HUD designed for deep-space missions where communication delays with Earth—up to 21 minutes one-way during Mars transit—prevent real-time ground support. Built on NASA-STD-3001 and NASA Human Research Program (HRP) standards, it monitors live vital signs via Web Bluetooth (BLE) or multi-parameter simulation—including heart rate with a dynamic ECG, blood pressure, SpO2, glucose, and sleep hours—alongside real-time exposure across NASA's 5 spaceflight hazards in Mars transit, orbital, lunar, and EVA environments.

Rather than evaluating metrics in isolation, its CIPHER-inspired Body Scanner dynamically connects affected organs whenever vitals become irregular, illustrating physiological cascades such as 0G fluid shifts driving SANS ocular pressure or bone loss increasing renal stone risk. The system also integrates a hybrid camera/ultrasound diagnostic scanner, daily HRP countermeasures paired with an average space nutrition plan (2,800–3,000 kcal, protein, Omega-3 lipids, and key vitamins), automated safety warnings for missed duties, and a 0G Emergency Assistant with a 110 BPM CPR metronome and solar storm radiation protocols (250 mSv single-event and 600 mSv career limits).

Replacing manual entries, Astrah Care features an autonomous logbook that self-evaluates every 2 minutes, cross-referencing vital sign trends, organ interconnections, and countermeasure compliance to produce timestamped diagnoses without crew intervention. By continuously correlating multi-system data over time, it generates new operational and scientific knowledge—detecting subtle physiological cascades onboard before they become emergencies, while building standardized, exportable longitudinal datasets (.TXT) that researchers can analyze post-mission to better model human adaptation and refine autonomous space medicine.
